key_inputs: Main polling anchors: self-funded Alpha Research, 18–22 October, n=1000, at 41.1/28.3/12.8; Trend for 24 Chasa, 14–20 October, n=1002, at 45.9/27.8/10.9; Myara for BNR, 8–19 October, n=1009, at 43.4/28.9/10.2.

Supporting polls: Market Links with bTV, 13–19 October, n=1006; self-funded Gallup, 14–22 October, n=1001; Sova Harris for Trud, 13–17 October, n=1000. Sova receives relatively little weight because of earlier fieldwork and its high Iotova readings, alongside its large pro-Radev outlier in 2021.

All forecasts use valid ballots including none. Market Links' candidate-only shares become approximately 45.5/29.4/9.9 after allowing its reported 3.8% none; Gallup's 2.2% undecided is not a ballot category, and its unusually low 0.4% none is given limited weight. Unclear denominators in other surveys add uncertainty.

In 2021, most final polls understated Radev by roughly 1–5 points and overstated Gerdzhikov by up to 5.5 points. April 2026 polls understated Progressive Bulgaria by roughly 10–14 points, although Market Links' adjusted forecast missed by less.

Progressive Bulgaria won 44.6% in April and backs Iotova alongside BSP and others. Every pollster reports a narrowing lead; late security controversies and uncertain choices by GERB/DPS voters limit confidence in a historical pro-Radev adjustment.

Registered-voter turnout estimates cluster around 39–40%; Trend's 47% uses resident adults and is not directly comparable. The forecast allows an upper turnout tail toward April's 50.7%, against approximately 6.59 million registered electors.

Markets are a low-weight cross-check: Iotova had approximately 95.5% probability of finishing first on 20 October, with only about $18,200 traded, while any outright first-round victory was approximately 3.7% on 22 October.

notes: The forecast gives greatest weight to recent fieldwork while allowing for differences in poll denominators, sponsors and historical performance. Iotova receives a modest upward adjustment for previous underestimation of the Radev electorate, tempered by the consistent narrowing across final polling waves. The 80% ranges allow substantial shared polling error, uncertain GERB/DPS voter transfers and a renewed mobilization surprise rather than treating survey sampling errors as total uncertainty. Expected turnout remains well below the threshold for an outright victory, making a runoff highly likely even if Iotova exceeds half of valid ballots. p_first denotes finishing first in this round, not winning the presidency outright.
